Let me think about this year's plan.

I have 40 mu total. Most of my land I do the wheat-maize rotation like everyone around here — that is what works on the plain. But I keep about 10 mu for cotton on the sandier plot by the south edge, because that ground does not hold water as well and cotton does alright there. So 30 mu is wheat-maize, 10 mu is cotton.

For **winter wheat** (30 mu): I plant Jimai 22 or something similar — the county seed dealer sells good improved varieties and my neighbors get 500 kg per mu easily. I put down compound fertilizer 15-15-15 before ploughing, about 50 kg per mu as base, then top-dress urea about 20-25 kg per mu at jointing in March. That gives me around 20 kg nitrogen total, 8 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium. Better to give a little extra than come up short — a weak wheat crop is a disaster. I irrigate four times: before winter, at jointing, at heading, and at grain filling. The well is reliable. Spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew, sometimes a third time if the weather is wet.

For **summer maize** (30 mu): No-till drill right into the wheat stubble after harvest — saves time and diesel, everyone does it now. Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, hybrid seed from the dealer. About 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 phosphorus, 5 potassium. One base application of compound fertilizer, then urea at big trumpet stage. Summer rain is usually enough but I irrigate once or twice if July is dry. Spray once for borers, sometimes twice. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

For **cotton** (10 mu): I use Bt hybrid seed — bollworm is still a problem without it. Plough this ground because cotton likes deeper soil. About 14 kg nitrogen, 6 phosphorus, 7 potassium per mu — cotton needs potassium for good bolls. Irrigate three times: after planting, at flowering, and at boll filling. Cotton needs many sprays — I do about 6 times for aphids, mites, and bollworm, also for the leaf pests. Cotton is more work but the price has been decent. I expect 270 kg seed cotton per mu.
